llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads project.code-workspace JSON and extracts folder basenames, handling both absolute and relative paths — VS Code auto-flushes workspace changes to disk, so this reliably reflects the post-action state.
File existence check via bash 'test -f' is robust and correctly detects /home/user/data1/notes.txt.
Metric awards 0.5 for each sub-goal (data1 in workspace folders + notes.txt exists), fully covering both instruction requirements.
Negative-control resistance is sound: initial state has data1 not in workspace and notes.txt absent, so initial score = 0.0.
Partial-credit structure is semantically correct — each sub-goal is independently verifiable and contributes equally.
The unused 'file_exists: true' field in expected.rules has no semantic impact since the metric reads file_exists directly from the getter result dict.
